analysis: The only change in this PR is a test-only addition in provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Service/ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift, at head lines 683-687 (base text lines 682-683 in the failedCommitPreservesMatchingHashAndFingerprint test). It adds assertions after a failed or unconfirmed model-switch commit. They check that loop.autopilotBusyReasons() does not contain .modelSwitch, and that .draining is present only when the connection dropped (dropConnection == true). No production source is modified, so no runtime behavior, trust boundary, key handling, attestation, encryption or cache-storage control changes. The assertions reinforce the intended fail-closed property: after an unconfirmed commit, refusingNewWork stays true and the drain is retained, while the switch task is released. This is consistent with TB-002 and with the T-053 lifecycle and drain concerns. The test uses a MockCoordinator and temporary directories, and touches no secrets. The other test content in the units is unchanged context. It exercises model-switch drain, hash-capture and rollback paths that were reviewed as existing behavior and are not new attack surface. Remaining questions: the production API autopilotBusyReasons() and its .modelSwitch and .draining reasons are outside the supplied evidence. I cannot confirm that the production state machine matches what the new assertions expect, but that is a test-correctness matter rather than a security regression.
